name: Taiwan Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)
description: Everything about Taiwan's Digital Nomad Visa: age-tiered income requirements, 2-year maximum stay, remote work rules, insurance, and step-by-step application. Updated for 2026.
keyRequirement: Remote work for overseas employer/clients + income ≥ USD $20K-40K/year (age-dependent)
targetAudience: Remote employees of companies headquartered outside Taiwan
Freelancers and independent contractors with global clients
Young digital professionals (20-29) seeking affordable Asia base
Experienced remote workers (30+) seeking Taiwan's infrastructure and safety

eligibility.label: Passport from a visa-exempt country
eligibility.description: Nationals from approximately 60+ visa-exempt countries and territories (across 90-day, 30-day, and 14-day categories) including US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Korea, and most EU countries. 14-day trial: Thailand, Brunei, Philippines (extended to July 31, 2026).

eligibility.label: Currently employed by overseas employer or operating freelance business with global clients
eligibility.description: Must be working for a company headquartered outside Taiwan or serving non-Taiwan clients as an independent contractor.

eligibility.label: Must NOT work for any Taiwan-based employer or company
eligibility.description: This is the most critical legal restriction. Violation may result in visa revocation, fines, and deportation. To work for a Taiwan employer, a separate Work Permit or Gold Card is required.

eligibility.label: Meet age-tiered annual income threshold
eligibility.description: Age 20-29: ≥ USD $20,000/year. Age 30+: ≥ USD $40,000/year. Previous DNV holders from other countries: income requirement waived. Must meet threshold for at least 1 of previous 2 years.

eligibility.label: Bank balance of at least USD $10,000 average over past 6 months
eligibility.description: Past 6 months average monthly balance must be ≥ USD $10,000. Bank statement required as proof.

eligibility.label: Comprehensive international health and hospitalization insurance
eligibility.description: Must cover the entire planned stay in Taiwan. DNV holders are excluded from Taiwan's National Health Insurance (NHI) — no exceptions. Policy must explicitly cover hospitalization.
warnings: DNV holders are excluded from Taiwan's National Health Insurance (NHI) — you must maintain private international health and hospitalization insurance at all times

fees.applicationDetail: NT$1,600 (single entry) or NT$3,200 (multiple entry) for domestic applications. USD $50 or $100 for overseas applications.
fees.notes: US citizens: NT$7,090 (domestic) or USD $185 (overseas) due to reciprocity surcharge. Application fees are non-refundable regardless of outcome.

incomeRequirement.notes: Age-tiered: 20-29 years = USD $20,000/year minimum. 30+ years = USD $40,000/year minimum. Holders of DNV from another country = income requirement waived. Must meet for at least 1 of previous 2 years. Separate bank balance requirement: 6-month average ≥ USD $10,000.

documents.name: Online Application Form
documents.description: Completed online application from visawebapp.boca.gov.tw, printed and signed
tips: Fill out completely online, then print and sign before submission

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must have 6+ months validity and blank visa pages. Color copy of photo page required.
tips: Temporary and emergency passports are NOT accepted
Japan and US passport holders only need passport valid for duration of stay

documents.name: Passport Photos
documents.description: 2 photos, 45x35mm, white background, taken within 6 months

documents.name: Resume or Professional Portfolio
documents.description: Detailed CV/resume showing education and work history, or professional portfolio demonstrating remote work capabilities

documents.name: Employment Contract or Project Contracts
documents.description: For employees: valid employment contract with overseas employer. For freelancers: active project contracts with global clients.
tips: Contract must clearly show the employer/client is based outside Taiwan
Freelancers should provide multiple project contracts

documents.name: Description of Intended Activities
documents.description: Detailed work plan for your stay in Taiwan — describe your projects, clients, and planned activities during the visa period
tips: Be specific about projects and clients — vague plans may be questioned
Explain how your work is performed remotely for overseas entities

documents.name: Income Proof / Tax Certificates
documents.description: Tax certificates (W-2, P60, T4, PAYG, etc.) or employer salary certificate proving age-tier income for at least 1 of previous 2 years
tips: Age 20-29: prove ≥ USD $20,000/year
Age 30+: prove ≥ USD $40,000/year
Previous DNV holders from other countries: income requirement waived — provide proof of other country's DNV instead

documents.name: Bank Statement
documents.description: Bank statement showing 6-month average monthly balance of at least USD $10,000
tips: Start maintaining $10K+ average 6 months BEFORE applying — last-minute deposits may not count
Use your primary bank account that shows consistent balance

documents.name: International Health Insurance Certificate
documents.description: Proof of comprehensive international health and hospitalization insurance covering the entire planned stay period
tips: SafetyWing, World Nomads, and Cigna Global are commonly used
Must explicitly cover Taiwan and include hospitalization
DNV holders are excluded from Taiwan's NHI — private insurance is mandatory

documents.name: Previous Country's DNV Proof
documents.description: If claiming income waiver based on holding a Digital Nomad Visa from another country, provide proof of that visa
tips: Accepted DNV countries include Thailand, Portugal, and others with digital nomad visa programs

applicationSteps.title: Check Eligibility
applicationSteps.description: Verify your visa-exempt nationality, age-tier income threshold, bank balance, overseas employment status, and insurance coverage.
tips: Use the BOCA website to confirm your country's visa-exempt status
Calculate your age tier: 20-29 = USD $20K, 30+ = USD $40K

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Documents
applicationSteps.description: Gather all required documents including employment contract, income proof, bank statements, insurance certificate, and activity plan.
tips: Start maintaining bank balance of $10K+ at least 6 months before application
No temporary or emergency passports accepted
Prepare a detailed activity plan — vague descriptions get questioned

applicationSteps.title: Complete Online Form
applicationSteps.description: Fill out the visa application at visawebapp.boca.gov.tw, print the completed form, and sign it.
tips: Double-check all information matches your passport exactly

applicationSteps.title: Submit Application
applicationSteps.description: Overseas: submit at your local ROC diplomatic mission (TECO or representative office). Domestic (already in Taiwan): submit at BOCA Taipei HQ or regional branches (Central, Southwest, South, East).
tips: Domestic applicants: MUST apply at least 10 business days before current stay expires
Overseas: check your jurisdictional TECO office for appointment requirements
warnings: Domestic applicants must apply at least 10 business days before current stay expires — overstay during processing is your responsibility

applicationSteps.title: NDC + BOCA Review
applicationSteps.description: National Development Council (NDC) reviews your eligibility, remote work credentials, and income. Upon NDC approval, BOCA processes the visa issuance.
tips: NDC focuses on verifying your remote work is genuinely overseas-based

applicationSteps.title: Receive Visa & Enter Taiwan
applicationSteps.description: Collect your visa from the issuing office and enter Taiwan within the visa validity period.
tips: Overseas: collect visa from the TECO/representative office that processed your application
Domestic: collect at BOCA Taipei or your regional branch

processingTime.notes: Faster than Gold Card. Domestic applicants: apply at least 10 business days before current stay expires to avoid overstay risk.

restrictions: ONLY for overseas employer/clients — absolutely NO Taiwan-based work
Cannot work for any Taiwan-registered company or entity
Cannot provide any form of labor or service to Taiwan-based businesses
To work for a Taiwan employer, must obtain separate Work Permit or Gold Card
ABSOLUTELY NO work for Taiwan-based employers — this is a visa violation that may result in revocation, fines, and deportation
workPermission.notes: This is the most critical legal restriction. Violation may result in visa revocation, fines, and deportation.

postArrivalSteps.title: ARC Application
postArrivalSteps.deadline: Within 30 days of arrival (for stays over 180 days)
postArrivalSteps.description: Apply for Alien Resident Certificate at the nearest NIA service center.
tips: Bring passport, visa, 2 photos, proof of address, and fees

agencySteps.agencyFullName: National Development Council (NDC, 國家發展委員會)
agencySteps.description: NDC reviews your income, employment status, and remote work credentials to verify eligibility.
tips: NDC focuses on verifying your remote work is genuinely overseas-based

agencySteps.agencyFullName: Bureau of Consular Affairs (外交部領事事務局)
agencySteps.description: BOCA processes and issues the Digital Nomad Visa upon NDC approval.
tips: Overseas: issued through local TECO/representative office
Domestic: collect at BOCA Taipei or regional office

faqs.question: Can I work for a Taiwan company on the Digital Nomad Visa?
faqs.answer: No. The DNV is exclusively for remote work for overseas employers/clients. Working for any Taiwan-based employer or entity is a visa violation.

faqs.question: What happens if I'm caught working for a Taiwan employer on DNV?
faqs.answer: Violation may result in visa revocation, fines, and deportation. Taiwan's Immigration Act enforces work restrictions strictly.

faqs.question: How does the age-based income requirement work?
faqs.answer: Age 20-29: minimum USD $20,000/year. Age 30+: minimum USD $40,000/year. Must meet the threshold for at least 1 of the previous 2 years. Holders of a DNV from another country have the income requirement waived.

faqs.question: What if I held a Digital Nomad Visa from another country?
faqs.answer: The income requirement is waived. Provide proof of your previous country's DNV (e.g., from Thailand, Portugal, etc.) with your application.

faqs.question: Can I extend my DNV beyond 6 months?
faqs.answer: Yes. Extensions are available in 6-month increments at NIA service centers. No need to leave Taiwan. Proof of residential address required.

faqs.question: What's the maximum stay on the Digital Nomad Visa?
faqs.answer: 2 years total (updated January 8, 2026). The initial visa is 6 months, extendable in 6-month increments.

faqs.question: Am I eligible for Taiwan's National Health Insurance (NHI) on DNV?
faqs.answer: No. DNV holders are explicitly excluded from Taiwan's NHI. You must maintain private international health and hospitalization insurance covering your entire stay.

faqs.question: What are the tax implications of staying in Taiwan on DNV?
faqs.answer: Three tiers: ≤90 days — minimal tax exposure (overseas-sourced income largely exempt). 91-183 days — remote work income performed in Taiwan becomes reportable, must file before departure. ≥183 days — full tax resident with progressive rates. High-income DNV holders planning 183+ day stays may want to check Gold Card eligibility for the 50% tax exemption benefit.

faqs.question: Can I bring my family on the Digital Nomad Visa?
faqs.answer: No. The DNV does not allow dependents. Family members would need to obtain their own visa status independently.

faqs.question: What happens if I overstay while my extension application is processing?
faqs.answer: You are responsible for any overstay. Domestic applicants must apply at least 10 business days before their current stay expires. Overstay during processing may result in visa denial and fines.

faqs.question: Can I switch from DNV to Gold Card?
faqs.answer: If you meet Gold Card qualification criteria in one of the 12 professional fields, you can apply for a Gold Card while on active DNV status in Taiwan. The Gold Card provides Taiwan work permission, NHI access, and tax benefits that the DNV does not.

faqs.question: What's the bank balance requirement?
faqs.answer: Your bank statement must show an average monthly balance of at least USD $10,000 over the past 6 months. This is separate from the income requirement. Start maintaining this balance well in advance — last-minute deposits may not be accepted.

tips: Apply at least 10 business days before your current visa-exempt stay expires to avoid overstay risk
Start maintaining your bank balance of $10K+ average at least 6 months before applying
Be very specific in your Activity Plan — NDC reviewers may question vague work descriptions
Budget for private health insurance throughout your stay — DNV holders have no NHI access
Join 'Digital Nomads Taiwan' and 'Expats in Taiwan' Facebook groups for community support
If planning to stay 183+ days, understand the tax implications — you may become a full tax resident

documents: Proof of residential address in Taiwan

pathsTo.name: Taiwan Employment Gold Card
pathsTo.requirements: Meet qualification criteria in one of 12 professional fields (salary ≥ NT$160,000/month, relevant experience, PhD, awards, etc.). Can apply while on active DNV status in Taiwan.
pathsTo.notes: The most common upgrade path for digital nomads who want Taiwan work permission, NHI access, and the 50% tax exemption benefit. Gold Card provides open work permit with no employer tie.

pathsTo.name: Work ARC (Employment-Sponsored)
pathsTo.requirements: Secure employment with a Taiwan-based company that sponsors your work permit. Employer must apply for the work permit before you can obtain the Work ARC.
pathsTo.notes: For DNV holders who find a Taiwan employer. Note: this means giving up remote work freedom — Work ARC ties you to the sponsoring employer. Requires a separate work permit from the Ministry of Labor.

pathsFrom.name: Visa-Exempt Entry / Visitor Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Passport from a visa-exempt country. Apply at BOCA office at least 10 business days before current visa-exempt stay expires.
pathsFrom.notes: The most common pathway. Enter Taiwan visa-exempt (up to 90 days for most countries), then apply for DNV conversion at a BOCA office. Also applies to holders of Digital Nomad Visas from other countries (income requirement waived — provide proof of previous DNV).
